To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the magnitude of trading prices affects the processing of information in experimental markets; (b) the effect is stronger between-participants than within-participants; and (c) the effect is consistent with the use of different scales to process small and large numbers in experimental markets.

(1) the magnitude of trading prices influences the way people process the distribution of returns; (2) the magnitude of prices influences the degree of mispricing in experimental markets; and (3) the effect of price magnitude is robust both within and between participants.

(1) the price magnitude of a stock affects the way participants process information in an experimental market; (2) the effect of price magnitude is stronger in the small price market than in the large price market; and (3) this effect occurs both between participants and within participants.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of price magnitude in the formation of beliefs and expectations.
how the magnitude of trading prices affects participants’ perceptions and, in turn, their behavior in a laboratory market.
the question of why small price markets exhibit greater overvaluation and greater mispricing than larger ones.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the magnitude of trading prices in financial markets matters.
the small price markets exhibit more mispricing than large ones.
(1) the law of small numbers is not only a law of statistics; and (2), it also applies to the way people process information about prices in financial markets.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
people process small numbers in a different way than large numbers, and this is reflected in the way they trade stocks.
small numbers are perceived as being less certain than large numbers, even when they are not.

, contrary to what is often assumed, the magnitude of prices is not irrelevant.
